lots.what_it_is: Boxed Mettoy Playthings (Swansea) tinplate model Hoover washing machine with hand-cranked mangle and side crank, 1950s, in its original printed 'Model Hoover Washing Machine' carton, plus a separate blue tubular steel school-style chair with ply seat.
lots.score_reason: A common British 1950s toy. The only price evidence is a UK auction estimate of GBP 10-20 for two boxed examples and an unverified eBay asking price. Machine itself looks clean, which helps, and the chair adds a little retro value, but the realistic local market is about $30-80 for the lot.

lots.key_photo_findings: Box end panel reads 'Made in Gt. Britain by the Mettoy Co. Ltd. Swansea' and 'Model HOOVER Registered Trade Mark of Hoover Ltd Washing Machine'. Machine is white tinplate with red 'HOOVER' badge, red crank handle on the side, chrome-handled mangle with red knob on top, grey top surround, black base. Paint looks bright with light rubbing and small rust or wear marks along the lower front edge and seams; a grey plate sits under it. Box is complete on four sides but the top flaps are torn away and the card is faded and soiled. Chair is a blue tubular steel stacking school chair with worn paint and a ply seat. No instruction leaflet visible.
lots.condition: Toy good with light wear and minor edge rust; box fair, top flaps missing; chair worn.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does the mangle turn and the side crank work? Is there any rust inside the tub or on the base, and is the grey plate underneath part of the toy? Are the box flaps and any instruction leaflet present?

lots.guide_summary: Close comparisons only: two Gowans plain ruby quantity lots sold at $37 and $50 hammer in 2026, and one similar lot passed in three times. Wider category guides (Venetian sets, Whitefriars, small ruby sets) sold $10-50 hammer. All sold, all AUD, no asking evidence found. Nothing is the same gold-fleck Murano style.
lots.working: Rule: maximum bids only from same-item SOLD. None of the Gowans lots is the same item (they are plain moulded ruby glasses, not Venetian aventurine-stem glasses), so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Indicative only, if you accept the close lots: lowest close SOLD $37 / 1.22 = $30.3, so about $30 hammer ($36.60 all-in). Flip: resale about $50 less 10% fees ($5) = $45, / 2.44 = $18.4, so about $15 hammer, not worth flipping.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark or label in the photos, maker unconfirmed, and the sold evidence is close or category only. Web search cap reached, so no Murano aventurine or Armitage past results could be checked.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All eight SOLD and the UNSOLD Gowans entries were re-checked against the live API (titles, sale_price, bid counts and listing dates all match). I viewed photos of 404978, 408323 and 409980: all plain red moulded goblets, confirming 'close' at best.
lots.key_photo_findings: Fifteen glasses: about 7 tall ovoid goblets and 8 wide coupes. Thin ruby bowls, clear twisted knops filled with gold aventurine fleck, clear round feet; looks hand-blown Venetian work. No label, etching or acid mark visible. No chips seen on rims or feet at this resolution, but rims are not shown close up.
lots.condition: Appears good, no chips seen, rims not inspected closely.
lots.question_for_armitage: Please check every rim and foot for chips or flea bites, and look for any foil label or acid-etched 'Murano' or 'Venezia' mark. How many glasses exactly (we count 15)?
